text:
maya: bump — seeing a 3x increase in 95th tail latency on prod GPU pool starting ~09:05 UTC, correlates with a drop in throughput. Noticing a pattern across two hosts.
liam: seen it too, visualizing right now. Any recent deploys?
evan: deploys were clear at 08:50. I pulled perf traces for the window.
maya: thanks. attaching quick summary: kernel selection flipped to int8_fallback on several long-sequence requests, batching heuristics produced large batches (n=48) which caused queueing. Also KV cache hit-rate dropped.
priya: oof — tool-calling customers? Could explain long sequences and cache misses.
maya: yes, one client had an infinite tool-calling loop that appended tool outputs to the prompt; start lengths jumped from ~512 to >6k tokens.
liam: can you paste the snippet from the profiler?
evan: sure — from the runtime logs:
```
[09:06:12] route=/api/v1/generate model=v1-7b variant=quant8 kernel=int8_fallback batch_size=48 seq_len=6200 avg_kernel_time=420ms
[09:06:13] kv_cache_hits=0.12 kv_cache_evictions=560
[09:06:14] gpu_util=92% pending_queue=120
```
maya: note the kernel switch — fallback kernel is 3-4x slower for these sequences. Kernel selector probed and chose based on expected memory usage; large seq -> fallback.
priya: also kv_cache_evictions high — sounds like thrashing. Maybe because requests switched model variants?
liam: I correlated client model pinning: some requests were routed to v1-7b-quant and others to v1-7b-quant8-lite due to a gradual rollout; different cache keys meant duplicates and evictions.
evan: confirmed. Two things happening together: prompt-length spike from tool loop + split model variants = KV cache fragmentation + larger batches by heuristic = queueing + fallback kernel.
maya: mitigation plan proposed: 1) emergency rate limit the offending token-streaming client (identified via token metadata). 2) force route long sequences to conservative small-batch path (cap batch size at 8 for seq_len > 2048). 3) temporarily pin to consistent model variant to restore cache locality.
priya: +1. Also we should add a streaming backpressure mechanism: if client ack is slow, don't let queue grow unbounded.
liam: rolling policy change: update batching heuristic to consider seq_len distribution and last-n acknowledgements. Quick patch:
```json
{"batching": {"max_batch_size": 64, "adaptive_rules": [{"seq_len_gt": 2048, "max_batch_size": 8}]}}
```
evan: applied the temporary routing pins and capped batches on two hosts. After 09:18 we see tail latency drop to ~1.2x baseline and throughput recovered.
infra-bot: deploy 1718004099 flagged: routing-pin applied to model v1-7b-quant on pool-prod-1 by evan.
maya: good catch. Remaining work: deeper kernel selector logs to see why fallback chosen even when quantized kernels could be used for parts of sequence; look into KV cache key scheme across model variants; and add alerting for prompt length spikes and repeated tool-call patterns.
liam: I'll open a follow-up with config diff and add a canary metric for kv_cache_eviction_rate.
priya: I'll draft the streaming backpressure RFC — suggest soft-window ACKs + per-connection token credits.
evan: for the incident postmortem, we should include: timeline, root cause (tool loop + variant fragmentation), mitigations, and long-term fixes (batching heuristics, kernel selector tuning, KV cache namespace alignment, streaming backpressure).
maya: marking resolved for now, but keep monitoring dashboards for 24h. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
